newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Kin Yat to run IPO from Apr 16 to 21 -sources.
newsitem.headline: HK's Kin Yat to run IPO from Apr 16 to 21 -sources.

text.p: The initial public offering (IPO) of shares in toy maker Kin Yat Holdings Ltd is expected to run from April 16 to 21 and dealing in the shares is expected to begin on May 1, market sources said on Wednesday.

Kin Yat is expected to issue 85 million new shares at HK$1.28 each, representing a price/earnings multiple of 6.3 times on a weighted average basis and 5.0 times on a fully-diluted basis, sources said.
Lippo Securities is the sponsor of the issue, sources added.

"The company forecasts a combined profit of HK$65 million for the year ended in March 1997, including an exceptional gain of HK$6.95 million," said an analyst who attended a company presentation on Wednesday.
"It posted a profit of HK$48 million for the eight months period to November 1996," another source said.
Kin Yat reported a profit of HK$30.3 million for the year ended in March 1996, up from HK$20.8 million in 1995 and HK$18.5 million in 1994, sources said.
Turnover was HK$233 million in 1996, up from HK$149 million in 1995 and HK$134 million in 1994, they said.
The Hong Kong-based company manufactures toy cars and electrical household appliances.

About 57 percent of the company's products were exported to the United States in the year ended March 1996, 21 percent to Europe, eight percent to Asia, and four percent to South America, sources said.
Kin Yat currently operates two production facilities in Baoan in China's southern province of Guangdong, they said.

Net proceeds of HK$96.80 million raised from the new issue will be used for construction of production facilities in Baoan, to buy machinery, upgrade equipment, develop products, and for general working capital, sources said.
